transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thanks for seeing me. I guess I’m here because things have been getting a little… overactive, maybe. I keep starting projects and plans—at work, certifications I want to do, upgrading stuff at home, even reaching out to old contacts—and I tell myself it’s productive, but then I kind of blow past normal limits. My wife or my director has had to step in and tell me to slow down, which is embarrassing. I’m not trying to cause problems, I just can’t seem to stop once I get going.
Do you often feel restless, like you can't sit still?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say all the time, but yes, pretty often lately. I’ll pace around the house with my laptop instead of just sitting at the desk, or I’ll end up reorganizing the garage or rewriting project boards when I probably could just leave them alone.

And if my wife wants to just sit and watch a show, I can do it for a bit, but I start feeling kind of physically uncomfortable, like I need to get up and do something. I know that probably sounds a little excessive.
Do you find it difficult to focus on one task for an extended period of time?

Yeah… I can focus sometimes, especially if it’s something urgent, but lately it’s been harder than I’d like to admit. It’s not that I don’t care about the task or anything.

Like, if I’m working on a report or trying to clear a ticket, something small will pull me off it—a phone buzz, the fan clicking, somebody walking past my office door—and my attention just snaps over there. Then I’ll realize I’ve drifted into something else and the original thing is still sitting there unfinished.

I don’t know if that’s normal stress or just me being scattered, but… yeah, it’s been noticeable.
Have you ever acted on impulse, doing something without thinking it through first?

I’m not sure I’d call it impulsive exactly… I mean, I try to be pretty responsible. But I guess there are times where I move faster than I probably should—like making decisions or starting something before I’ve really thought through the practical side.

Usually I can justify it to myself in the moment, like, “This makes sense, this will be useful.” Then later I might realize I should’ve paused or asked someone first. Nothing too dramatic, I don’t think… but yeah, maybe a little. Does that count as impulsive?
Are these behaviors and feelings causing problems for you at work or in your relationships?

Yeah… I mean, I wish I could say it’s not, but it has caused some problems.

Work has been the biggest one. After a migration I was responsible for didn’t go well, they put me on leave. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m blaming everything on this, because I know I’m accountable, but… my follow-through and judgment haven’t been what they should be.

At home, too, my wife has had to step in more than she should—around spending, and when I’m working late at night, and sometimes conversations that start normal but turn into arguments because I’m not… slowing down enough, I guess.

And I’ve kind of pulled back from things I used to be dependable for, like church music, climbing, mentoring. I still care about those things, I just haven’t been able to reliably show up or follow through. So… yeah, I guess it’s affecting more than I wanted to admit.
How long have you been experiencing these feelings of restlessness and difficulty focusing?

Um… I think it’s been going on longer than I wanted to admit. The more noticeable stretches—where I’m kind of unusually driven, not sleeping much, and feeling maybe too confident about what I can handle—have been happening for about a year and eight months or so.

I don’t know if I’m describing that the right way, but that’s probably the honest timeline.
Do you experience intense mood swings, where you quickly shift between feeling very happy or very irritable?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t know if I’d call them “mood swings” exactly, but there are weeks where I feel really up—almost electric, like I can handle anything and I’m moving faster than usual.

And then, honestly, it doesn’t take much for me to get irritated. Like if there’s a small delay, or my wife asks me a question that should be totally reasonable, I can snap and feel like people are trying to slow me down on purpose. I know that probably sounds bad… I’m not proud of it. But yes, that does happen.
Do you often find yourself easily distracted by your surroundings, even when you're trying to focus on something?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say every second, but it happens more than it should.

If my phone buzzes, or the fan clicks, or someone walks past my office door, my attention just kind of snaps to it. And then I’ll realize I’ve stopped working on the report or ticket I was supposed to finish. Sometimes I can get back to it, but other times I’m already off on something else.

I know everyone gets distracted, so I don’t want to overstate it… but yes, it’s been pretty noticeable.
Have you ever done something reckless or risky without thinking, like excessive spending or reckless driving?

Um… I don’t think so? Not in any big, obvious way.

I mean, I can be impulsive sometimes, like deciding I need to do something right away or getting a little too eager about a plan, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been out driving dangerously or spending huge amounts of money or anything like that. At least… not that I can point to as reckless.

Does that answer it okay?
Are you having difficulty performing daily tasks or maintaining a regular routine because of these feelings and behaviors?

Yeah… I guess it has affected things more than I’d like to admit.

At work, the big one is I was put on leave after a migration failed. I don’t want to make it sound like I was the only factor, but… I know my stuff wasn’t where it needed to be, and it got serious enough that I’m not there right now.

At home, my wife has had to step in more than she should—around spending decisions, me working late into the night, and just conversations that start normal but turn into arguments. I don’t mean for that to happen, but it does.

And I’ve kind of pulled back from things I used to be dependable for, like church music, climbing, and mentoring. I’ll say I’m going to show up or follow through, and then I just… don’t reliably do it. So yes, it’s interfering. I’m trying not to overstate it, but it’s there.
Have you been experiencing any physical complaints, such as headaches or stomachaches, alongside these feelings and behaviors?

Not really, no. I mean… I get the normal stuff now and then, like anyone, but I haven’t noticed headaches or stomachaches being a regular part of it.

I don’t want to miss something if it matters, but nothing physical is standing out to me like that.
Have you noticed any significant strain on your relationship with your wife due to your recent behaviors?

Yeah… yes, there has been strain. I wish I could say it’s just normal marriage stress, but I think my recent behavior has put more on her than is fair.

She’s had to step in around spending decisions, and when I’m working late into the night, that affects her too. And conversations that should be simple… they can turn into arguments, even when I’m not trying to make them that way.

I’ve also been less dependable with things outside the house, like church music, climbing, mentoring—things I used to follow through on better—and I think that adds to the pressure at home. And with being put on leave after that migration failed, that’s been hanging over us too.

So… yeah, it’s strained things. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I know it’s been hard on her.
Have these feelings and behaviors been consistently present over the past year and eight months, or have they come and gone?

They’ve come and gone some, but… if I’m being honest, those unusually driven periods—where I’m sleeping less and feeling more confident than I probably should—have been part of things for about a year and eight months.

I don’t mean it’s been every single day nonstop. But it’s been there across that whole stretch, in waves, I guess. Does that make sense?
Have you experienced significant symptoms of inattention or hyperactivity-impulsivity prior to the age of 12?

I’m not really sure… I don’t think so, at least not in any major way.

I mean, I was a kid, so I’m sure I got distracted or restless like anyone, but I don’t remember it being a significant problem before 12. I don’t recall teachers or my parents making a big issue of it.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Did you have difficulty sitting still or paying attention in class when you were a child?

Not that I really remember, no. I mean, I probably had normal kid moments where I got bored or fidgeted, but I don’t remember it being a big issue in class.

I don’t think teachers were calling home about me not sitting still or anything like that. At least… not that I know of. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Did you exhibit any of these restless or inattentive behaviors before you were a teenager?

I don’t think so, no. Not in a way that stands out to me.

Before I was a teenager, I think I was pretty much okay in school—maybe normal boredom or fidgeting sometimes, but nothing that I remember as a real pattern. I’m not aware of anyone saying I had a problem with attention or restlessness back then. Is that helpful?
Did you often have trouble following through on instructions or finishing homework when you were a kid, before you turned 12?

I don’t really remember that being a frequent problem before I was 12. I mean, I’m sure there were times I didn’t want to do homework or had to be reminded, like most kids, but I don’t think it was often or serious.

I don’t recall getting in trouble a lot for not finishing assignments or not following instructions. At least, nothing that stands out to me now. Is that specific enough?
Have you experienced these difficulties with restlessness, focus, and impulsivity in multiple areas of your life, such as at work, at home, and in social situations?

Yeah… I think it’s shown up in more than one place, unfortunately. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m just out of control or something, but it has affected work and home.

At work, things got bad after a migration failed, and I was put on leave. At home, my wife has had to step in more than I’d like to admit—around spending, me working late into the night, and conversations turning into arguments.

And socially, I’ve kind of pulled back from things I used to be involved in, like church music, climbing, and mentoring, because I can’t always reliably show up or follow through. So… yes, I guess it’s been across different parts of my life. Does that answer it okay?
Did you have any problems with paying attention or sitting still when you were in elementary school?

Not that I can really remember, no. In elementary school I think I was pretty typical—maybe I got bored sometimes or wiggled around like kids do, but I don’t remember it being a real issue.

I wasn’t, like, constantly getting in trouble for not paying attention or not sitting still, at least not that I know of. If there was something, it didn’t stand out enough that I remember it now. Does that answer what you’re looking for?
Do you remember having trouble paying attention or sitting still when you were really young, like before you were 7 years old?

Honestly, I don’t really remember anything like that from before age 7. That’s pretty young, so I’m mostly going off what I can recall and what family stories I’ve heard, and nothing really stands out.

I think I was probably an active kid like anyone else, but I don’t remember it being a problem, like teachers or my parents constantly saying I couldn’t sit still or pay attention. So… I’d say no, not that I know of. Is that okay?

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity have been consistently present over the past year and eight months, causing significant problems in multiple areas of life, including work and relationships. However, the patient does not meet the full criteria for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Predominantly Inattentive Type (F90.0) or Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Other Specified Type (F90.8), as the symptoms did not have an onset prior to age 12.
